Name: Clean Product
Qualities to look for: Brighter whites, open object shadows and restrained texture. Compare the background and shadow detail on the camera body.

Name: Fine Art & Pigments
Qualities to look for: A modest paper-white lift and clearer paper texture. Compare pigment hues and the lightest washes. Start with a neutral capture.

Name: Punchy
Qualities to look for: More midtone contrast and color separation, with legible shadows. Look at the faces of buildings and the brighter signs.

Name: Portrait 400
Qualities to look for: Soft highlight roll-off, a small shadow lift and restrained color around skin. Fine, soft-edged grain.

Name: Gold 200
Qualities to look for: Amber warmth, rich red and yellow details and fine grain. Compare the warmer facades and the color of the sky.

Name: Pastel 400
Qualities to look for: Brighter lower midtones, muted greens and blues, cooler shadows and a faint pink highlight tint. Fine, soft-edged grain.

Name: Vivid 100
Qualities to look for: Saturated reds and clear blues with fine grain. Compare with Vivid Slide for more open shadows.

Name: Vivid Slide
Best for: Sunlit landscapes and bold natural color
Qualities to look for: Deep blues and greens, firm shadows and crisp highlight separation. Look at the valley and the clouds.

Name: Chrome 64
Qualities to look for: Richer brick reds and deeper blues, with more subdued greens and overall saturation than Vivid Slide. Fine grain.

Name: Tungsten 800T
Best for: Mixed-light streets and bright practical lights
Qualities to look for: Cool shadows, visible fine-textured grain and red-orange halation around the brightest signs. The glow depends on nearby dark tones.

Name: Expired
Qualities to look for: Fogged blacks, a green-to-pink color shift and uneven-looking coarse grain. Age and storage give real expired film a wide range of looks.

Name: Instant
Qualities to look for: Creamy highlights, raised blacks, soft contrast and darker corners. Compare the face and the frame edges.

Name: Neutral
Best for: A plain starting point for monochrome
Qualities to look for: Even grayscale with Atelier's default B&W Mix. Check that there's no added curve, grain or toning when applied to a reset photo.

Name: Silver Gelatin
Qualities to look for: Dense shadows, bright whites and a barely visible cool-shadow and warm-highlight split. Look for detail in the pale rock.

Name: Classic 400
Qualities to look for: Crisp detail, a mild yellow-filter effect and visible classic grain. Compare the sky and the building surfaces.

Name: Push 400
Qualities to look for: Coarse grain, strong contrast and harder shadows than Classic 400. Inspect grain at 100%.

Name: Dark Sky
Qualities to look for: Blue sky and cyan tones darken while warm rock and clouds stay bright. The effect depends on the original sky color.

Name: Infrared Glow
Qualities to look for: Greens and yellows become lighter, blues turn very dark, and bright edges bloom softly. The recipe works from visible colors.

Name: Selenium
Qualities to look for: Dense blacks with a faint plum shift in the darker tones and near-neutral highlights. Compare with the warmer Sepia.

Name: Sepia
Qualities to look for: Chocolate-brown shadows, warm midtones and lighter cream highlights. Look for warmth across the grayscale image.

Name: Natural Skin
Qualities to look for: Gently reduced reds and oranges, a small lift in skin mids, and slightly softer texture. Compare cheeks and hands.

Name: Bright & Airy
Qualities to look for: Lifted skin mids and open shadows, lighter surrounding colors, and recognizable dark tones. Look at the face and dark fabric.

Name: Soft Glow
Best for: Backlit portraits and soft window light
Qualities to look for: Gentle diffusion and softer texture with warm light spilling at bright edges. Compare the cheek highlights and edge detail.

Name: Rich Skin
Qualities to look for: Open shadows and restrained golden warmth. Look for definition in the face without a strong red or yellow shift.

Name: Clean Studio
Qualities to look for: Crisper tonal separation with controlled skin saturation and clean light areas. Compare fabric and facial texture.

Name: Moody Portrait
Qualities to look for: Deeper surroundings and subdued background color with warmer skin mids. The vignette concentrates attention toward the center.

Name: Dramatic Sky
Qualities to look for: A darker blue sky and more cloud texture, with less pressure on foreground shadows. Inspect the ridgelines for halos.

Name: Golden Hour
Best for: Already warm side light and late-day landscapes
Qualities to look for: Amber sunlit rock and vegetation, with cooler shadow separation. Compare the lit cliff to the sky.

Name: Blue Hour
Best for: Twilight and city scenes with warm lights
Qualities to look for: Cobalt-blue midtones and deeper shadows separate warm practical lights from the cooler surroundings. The strongest fit is an already cool scene.

Name: Deep Greens
Qualities to look for: Deeper pine greens, darker foliage shadows and warmer shafts of light. Compare the green leaves to the lit path.

Name: Autumn Colors
Best for: Woodland with yellow and turning foliage
Qualities to look for: Yellow-green foliage leans toward amber and existing oranges and reds become stronger. Compare leaves and bark.

Name: Haze Cut
Qualities to look for: Stronger distant contrast and clearer ridgelines. Check the horizon edge and reduce Amount on already clear air.

Name: Wildlife & Detail
Qualities to look for: More fine subject texture, brighter warm details and more subdued surroundings. Compare the wing feathers and beak.

Name: Muted Chrome
Qualities to look for: Reduced blue and green saturation, firm shadows and restrained color that leaves reds readable. Compare the signs and the sky.

Name: Hard Light
Best for: Direct sunlight and graphic street scenes
Qualities to look for: Deep shadow shapes and bold primary colors. Check separation in the street shadows before raising Amount.

Name: Copper Negative
Best for: Daylight street with warm brick and cool pavement
Qualities to look for: Contrasting copper reds and cyan-slate shadows, with visible classic grain. Compare warm signs to cool surfaces.

Name: Teal & Orange
Qualities to look for: Teal-biased darks and warm orange mids, with less emphasis on greens. Check skin before increasing Amount.

Name: Bleach Bypass
Qualities to look for: Hard darks, metallic highlights and color muted enough to approach monochrome. Compare the remaining colors in signs and vehicles.

Name: Noir
Qualities to look for: Deep black-and-white contrast, bright pools of light and darker corners. Look at bright signage and shadowed edges.

Name: Night City
Qualities to look for: Stronger cyan and magenta accents with deeper midnight shadows. Check that bright sign detail remains legible.

Name: Warm Drama
Qualities to look for: Bronze shadows and ochre midtones with less blue and green saturation. Compare sunlit rock and the subdued cool colors.

Name: Faded Matte
Qualities to look for: Lifted charcoal blacks and softer highlights with some midtone contrast. Look at the deepest shadows for a restrained cast.

Name: Seventies
Best for: Retro snapshots and warm street color
Qualities to look for: Mustard yellows, terracotta reds, softened blues and lightly faded blacks. Compare street signage and pale walls.

Name: Midcentury Postcard
Best for: Travel views with blue sky and warm details
Qualities to look for: Soft turquoise blues, coral warmth and gently lifted shadows. Compare the sky with the sunlit rock.

Name: Cross Process
Qualities to look for: Strong green-cyan shadows and yellow highlights from deliberately skewed color curves. Compare pale facades and the color of shadowed surfaces.
